paragraphs: We are a clinical stage biotechnology company advancing optimized, novel biologics with the potential for differentiated efficacy and dosing in the largest inflammatory and immunology ("I&I") markets, including for the treatment of atopic dermatitis ("AD"), asthma, eosinophilic esophagitis ("EoE"), chronic obstructive pulmonary disease ("COPD"), and other I&I indications. Our antibody programs are designed to overcome limitations of existing therapies by targeting well-established mechanisms of action and incorporating advanced antibody engineering to optimize half-life and other properties.

Our pipeline comprises multiple antibody programs being developed initially for the treatment of I&I indications as monotherapies and combinations, including zumilokibart (APG777), APG279 (zumilokibart + APG990), APG273 (zumilokibart + APG333), and APG808 (each, a "program" or "product candidate"). With four validated targets in our portfolio, we are seeking to achieve best-in-class efficacy and dosing through monotherapies and combinations of our novel antibodies. Based on a broad pipeline and depth of expertise, we believe we can deliver value and meaningful benefit to patients underserved by today's standard of care. We believe each of our product candidates has potential for broad application across multiple I&I indications.

We have multiple clinical programs in our pipeline based on four validated targets being developed initially for the treatment of I&I indications, as shown below. We believe each of our programs has potential for broad application across multiple I&I indications.

The agents listed above are currently under investigation. Their safety and effectiveness have not yet been established by any regulatory authority. APG808 (not shown) is a novel half-life extended IL-4Rα antibody. Apogee announced positive interim results from the Phase 1b trial of APG808 in patients with mild-to-moderate asthma in May 2025.

1 APG279 is a combination of zumilokibart (APG777) and APG990. APG279 will be co-administered in the proof-of-concept Phase 1b trial; coformulation planned for future clinical studies and commercialization.
2 APG273 is a combination of zumilokibart and APG333.
Zumilokibart is a subcutaneous ("SQ") extended half-life monoclonal antibody ("mAb") targeting IL-13.

In August 2023, we initiated a Phase 1 trial of zumilokibart in healthy volunteers. The zumilokibart Phase 1 trial was a double-blind, placebo-controlled study in healthy volunteers and consisted of a single-ascending dose ("SAD") component and a multiple ascending dose component. Eight healthy volunteers, six treated with zumilokibart and two treated with placebo, were enrolled in each cohort, and we enrolled a total of 40 healthy adult subjects in the trial.

In March 2024, we announced positive interim safety and PK data from this trial with zumilokibart demonstrating a potential best-in-class PK profile, including a half-life of 77 days, supporting the potential for every three- to six- month maintenance dosing in AD. Single doses of zumilokibart demonstrated a deep and sustained effect on PD markers out to approximately 12 months. Zumilokibart was well-tolerated across all dose groups.

In May 2024, we announced dosing of our first patient in the APEX Phase 2 clinical trial, which is a randomized, placebo-controlled study evaluating zumilokibart in patients with moderate-to-severe AD.

In July 2025, we announced positive 16-week data from the Part A portion of the APEX Phase 2 clinical trial. Part A of the trial enrolled 123 adult patients who were randomized 2:1 to zumilokibart versus placebo and received an induction regimen dosing of 720mg at Weeks 0 and 2, followed by 360mg at Weeks 4 and 12. The primary endpoint for the induction arm of Part A was percentage change in Eczema Area Severity Index ("EASI") score from baseline at Week 16. Secondary endpoints included EASI-75, EASI-90, Validated Investigator Global Assessment ("vIGA") 0/1 and Itch Numeric Rating Scale ("NRS") at Week 16. In non-head-to-head trial comparisons, the initial 16-week findings from Part A included efficacy results, which compared favorably versus standard of care across endpoints, as well as rapid onset of itch relief and lesion reduction, and a favorable safety profile consistent with its class.

The Part A trial met its primary endpoint, with zumilokibart showing significantly greater least squares mean percent change from baseline at Week 16 with an EASI reduction of 71.0% compared to placebo of 33.8% (p < 0.001). Zumilokibart showed the highest absolute and placebo-adjusted EASI-75 of any biologic in a 16-week global study with 66.9% of patients treated with zumilokibart achieving EASI-75 compared to 24.6% on placebo (p < 0.001). Pre-specified sensitivity analysis showed consistent results in both moderate and severe patients based on baseline EASI score. The results demonstrated a vIGA 0/1 of 34.9% compared to placebo of 17.3% (p < 0.05) and an EASI-90 of 33.9% compared to placebo of 14.7% (p < 0.05). Treatment of patients with zumilokibart led to rapid and deep onset of itch relief and achieved a statistically significant reduction by Week 1, with a 50.7% reduction of Itch NRS from baseline compared to placebo of 23.2% (p < 0.01) at Week 16. Zumilokibart was well tolerated, with 56.1% of zumilokibart -exposed patients experiencing treatment-emergent adverse events ("TEAEs") (vs. 63.4% in placebo). The most common TEAEs, occurring in more than 5% of patients, were non-infective conjunctivitis (14.6% vs. 2.4% in placebo), upper respiratory tract infection (8.5% vs 12.2% in placebo), nasopharyngitis (4.9% vs. 12.2% in placebo), and pain in extremity (0.0% vs. 7.3% in placebo) with the latter three being numerically lower in zumilokibart treated patients compared to placebo. Serious TEAEs were rare for zumilokibart -exposed patients (1.2% vs. 2.4% in placebo). The discontinuation rate due to adverse events was low for zumilokibart -exposed patients (2.4%). There were no injection site reactions in the zumilokibart treated group. In addition, improvement in asthma and sinusitis, as measured by improvements in ACQ-5 and SNOT-22 in patients with comorbid asthma or sinusitis, was observed, which reflect zumilokibart's potential to broadly impact Type 2 inflammatory disease.

All Part A patients that benefited from treatment in the induction arm received the opportunity to continue to zumilokibart maintenance treatment, which evaluated three and six-month dosing intervals. Patients in the placebo arm for the first 16 weeks also received the opportunity to receive an induction regimen of zumilokibart followed by three-month dosing of zumilokibart. A schematic of the Part A trial design is shown in Figure 1 below. We expect to report Part A maintenance data in March 2026.
In February 2025, we announced that we had commenced dosing of the Part B portion of the APEX Phase 2 trial. Part B is testing a higher and a lower dose of zumilokibart.

paragraphs: Investing in our common stock involves a high degree of risk. Before you decide to invest in our common stock, you should consider carefully the risks described below, together with the other information contained in this Annual Report, including "Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations" and our audited consolidated financial statements and related notes. We believe the risks described below are the risks that are material to us as of the date of this Annual Report. Some of the factors, events and contingencies discussed below may have occurred in the past, but the disclosures below are not representations as to whether or not the factors, events or contingencies have occurred in the past, and instead reflect our beliefs and opinions as to the factors, events, or contingencies that could materially and adversely affect us in the future. If any of the following risks actually occur, our business, financial condition, results of operations and future growth prospects could be materially and adversely affected. In these circumstances, the market price of our common stock could decline, and you may lose all or part of your investment.

Below is a summary of the material risks to our business, our operations and an investment in our common stock. This summary does not address all of the risks that we face. Risks and uncertainties not presently known to us or that we presently deem less significant may also impair our business operations. Additional discussion of the risks summarized in this risk factor summary, and other risks that we face, can be found below and should be carefully considered, together with other information in this Annual Report in its entirety before making investment decisions regarding our common stock.

• We are a clinical stage biotechnology company with a limited operating history, we are currently conducting clinical trials, and we have no products approved for commercial sale, which may make it difficult for you to evaluate our current business and likelihood of success and viability.

• We will require substantial additional capital to finance our operations in the future. If we are unable to raise such capital when needed, or on acceptable terms, we may be forced to delay, reduce and/or eliminate one or more of our development programs or future commercialization efforts.

• We have incurred significant losses since inception, and we expect to incur significant losses for the foreseeable future and may not be able to achieve or sustain profitability in the future. We have no products approved for sale, have not generated any revenue from our programs and may never generate revenue or become profitable.
• We face competition from entities that have developed or may develop programs for the diseases addressed by our programs.

On October 10, 2025, pursuant to our Registration Statement on Form S-3, which became effective in August 2024 (File No 333-281503), we issued and sold an aggregate of 8,048,782 shares of common stock (inclusive of 1,097,561 shares of common stock pursuant to the exercise in full of the underwriters' option to purchase additional shares) at a public offering price of $41.00 per share, and, in lieu of common stock to certain investors, pre-funded warrants to purchase up to 365,853 shares of common stock at a public offering price of $40.99999 per pre-funded warrant (the "October 2025 Offering"). paragraphs: 本公司為一家臨牀階段生物科技公司，致力於開發經過優化、具創新性的生物製劑，這些製劑在最大的發炎與免疫學（"I&I"）市場中，具有差異化的療效與用藥劑量潛力，包括治療過敏性皮膚炎（"AD"）、氣喘、嗜酸性粒細胞食道炎（"EoE"）、慢性阻塞性肺病（"COPD"）及其他I&I適應症。我們的單克隆抗體計畫設計用以克服現有療法的限制，透過針對已建立的作用機制，並結合先進的抗體工程技術，以優化半衰期及其他特性。

我們的產品線包含多個抗體計畫，這些計畫最初是用來開發用於治療I&I適應症的單一療法與組合療法，包括zumilokibart（APG777）、APG279（zumilokibart + APG990）、APG273（zumilokibart + APG333）以及APG808（每項，為"計畫"或"產品候選品"）。我們產品線中有四個已驗證的目標，我們正尋求透過單一療法與組合療法，實現最佳等級的療效與用藥劑量。基於廣泛的產品線與深厚的專業知識，我們相信我們可以為目前標準照護未充分服務的患者帶來價值與有意義的效益。我們相信每項產品候選品都有潛力應用於多個I&I適應症。
我們的產品線中有許多臨牀計畫，這些計畫基於四個已驗證的目標，最初是用來開發用於治療I&I適應症，如下所示。我們相信每項計畫都有潛力應用於多個I&I適應症。
上述列出的藥物目前仍在研究階段。其安全性與有效性尚未經任何監管機構確認。APG808（未顯示）為一種新型半衰期延長的IL-4Rα抗體。Apogee於2025年5月宣佈APG808在輕度至中度氣喘患者中的Phase 1b試驗取得積極的中期結果。
1 APG279為zumilokibart（APG777）與APG990的組合。APG279將在概念驗證Phase 1b試驗中共同給藥；預計未來臨牀試驗與商業化時會進行共同配方。
2 APG273為zumilokibart與APG333的組合。
Zumilokibart為一種皮下（"SQ"）半衰期延長的單克隆抗體（"mAb"），針對IL-13。
2023年8月，我們啟動了zumilokibart的Phase 1試驗，對象為健康志工。zumilokibart的Phase 1試驗為一項雙盲、安慰劑對照試驗，對象為健康志工，試驗包含單次劑量遞增（"SAD"）組分與多次劑量遞增組分。每組有八位健康志工，其中六位接受zumilokibart治療，兩位接受安慰劑治療，總共納入40位健康成人受試者。
2024年3月，本公司宣佈本試驗中zumilokibart的臨牀安全與藥代動力學（PK）數據為正面，顯示其具有潛在最佳等級的PK特性，包括半衰期為77天，支持每三至六個月維持劑量使用的潛力。zumilokibart單次劑量顯示對PD指標有深層且持續的影響，持續約12個月。zumilokibart在所有劑量組別中皆具有良好耐受性。
2024年5月，本公司宣佈在APEX第二期臨牀試驗中，首名受試者開始接受zumilokibart治療，該試驗為隨機、安慰劑對照試驗，評估zumilokibart在中度至重度AD患者中的療效。

2025年7月，本公司宣佈來自APEX第二期臨牀試驗第一階段（Part A）的16週正面數據。第一階段試驗納入123名成人患者，隨機以2:1比例分為zumilokibart組與安慰劑組，並接受誘導劑量治療，於第0週與第2週給予720mg，隨後於第4週與第12週給予360mg。第一階段的首要終點為第16週時與基線相比的Eczema Area Severity Index（"EASI"）分數變化百分比。次要終點包括第16週的EASI-75、EASI-90、Validated Investigator Global Assessment（"vIGA"）0/1及Itch Numeric Rating Scale（"NRS"）。在非頭對頭試驗比較中，第一階段的初步16週結果顯示療效結果優於標準照護，且具有快速止癢與皮膚病竈減少的效果，並具有與其類別一致的優良安全性。

第一階段試驗達成其首要終點，zumilokibart在第16週時與基線相比的最小平方均數變化百分比顯著高於安慰劑，EASI減少71.0%對比安慰劑的33.8%（p < 0.001）。zumilokibart在16週全球試驗中，顯示最高的絕對值與安慰劑調整後的EASI-75，有66.9%接受zumilokibart治療的患者達成EASI-75，對比安慰劑的24.6%（p < 0.001）。預設的敏感性分析顯示，在基線EASI分數為中度或重度的患者中，結果一致。結果顯示vIGA 0/1為34.9%對比安慰劑的17.3%（p < 0.05），以及EASI-90為33.9%對比安慰劑的14.7%（p < 0.05）。接受zumilokibart治療的患者在第1週即顯示快速且深層的癢感緩解，並在第16週達到統計顯著的減少，Itch NRS減少50.7%對比安慰劑的23.2%（p < 0.01）。zumilokibart具有良好耐受性，有56.1%接受zumilokibart治療的患者出現治療相關不良事件（"TEAEs"）（對比安慰劑的63.4%）。最常見的TEAEs，發生率超過5%的為非感染性結膜炎（14.6% vs. 2.4%在安慰劑組）、上呼吸道感染（8.5% vs. 12.2%在安慰劑組）、鼻咽炎（4.9% vs. 12.2%在安慰劑組），以及肢體疼痛（0.0% vs. 7.3%在安慰劑組），後三者在zumilokibart治療組中數值較低。zumilokibart治療組的嚴重TEAEs為罕見（1.2% vs. 2.4%在安慰劑組）。因不良事件而中止治療的比率在zumilokibart治療組中為低（2.4%）。zumilokibart治療組未觀察到注射部位反應。此外，在患有過敏性鼻炎或鼻竇炎的患者中，觀察到哮喘與鼻竇炎改善，以ACQ-5與SNOT-22的改善為衡量，這反映zumilokibart具有廣泛影響Type 2發炎疾病的潛力。
所有在誘導臂中受益於治療的第一階段患者都有機會繼續接受zumilokibart維持治療，評估三與六個月的劑量間隔。在第一階段的安慰劑組患者也都有機會接受zumilokibart的誘導劑量治療，隨後接受三月劑量的zumilokibart治療。第一階段試驗設計的示意圖如圖1所示。本公司預期於2026年3月報告第一階段的維持治療數據。
2025年2月，本公司宣佈已開始進行APEX第二期試驗的第二階段（Part B）的劑量治療。第二階段正在測試zumilokibart的較高與較低劑量。

您應配合本年度報告書（Form 10-K）中所附的合併財務報表及相關附註，閱讀下列關於我們財務狀況與營運成果的討論。下列討論包含前瞻性陳述，反映我們目前的計畫、預測、估計與信念，並涉及風險與不確定性。我們的歷史財務表現未必能作為預測未來期間財務表現的依據。我們的實際結果、結果與事件的時間點，可能與前瞻性陳述中所討論的有重大差異。導致這些差異的因素包括下列所討論的內容及其他本年度報告書中所提及的內容，特別是在「特別提醒前瞻性陳述」與「風險因素」部分。我們建議您謹慎考慮這些因素，以評估本年度報告書中所包含的前瞻性陳述。前瞻性陳述並非歷史事實，反映我們對未來事件的當前觀點，僅適用於陳述當日。我們不預期，也無義務更新這些前瞻性陳述，除非法律有此要求。除非上下文另有明確要求，否則提及「我們」、「我們」、「我們」、「Apogee」或「本公司」均指 Apogee Therapeutics, Inc. 及其子公司。

我們是一家臨牀階段的生物科技公司，致力於開發優化且創新之生物製劑，這些製劑在最大的發炎與免疫學（"I&I"）市場中，具有差異化的療效與用藥方式，包括用於治療過敏性皮膚炎（"AD"）、氣喘、嗜酸性粒細胞食道炎（"EoE"）、慢性阻塞性肺病（"COP, 以及其它 I&I 指標。我們的單克隆抗體計畫設計用以克服現有療法的限制，透過針對已建立的作用機制，並結合先進的單克隆抗體工程技術，以優化半衰期及其他特性。

我們的產品線包含多個單克隆抗體計畫，這些計畫最初是為治療 I&I 指標而開發，作為單一療法或組合療法，包括 zumilokibart (APG777)、APG279 (zumilokibart + APG990)、APG273 (zumilokibart + APG333) 以及 APG808（每項均為一 "計畫" 或 "產品候選品"）。我們的產品線中有四個已驗證的目標，我們正努力透過單一療法或組合療法，實現我們創新單克隆抗體的最佳療效與用藥方式。基於廣泛的產品線與專業深度，我們相信我們能為目前標準照護未充分服務的患者帶來價值與顯著的效益。我們相信我們的每個產品候選品都有潛力在多個 I&I 指標中廣泛應用。

於2025年10月10日，根據我們於2024年8月生效的Form S-3登記聲明書（檔號333-281503），我們發行並出售總計8,048,782股普通股（包含因行使經理人選擇權而購買額外股份的1,097,561股普通股），發行價格為每股41.00美元，並針對部分投資者以預先資助的選擇權取代普通股，發行預先資助的選擇權，可購買最高365,853股普通股，發行價格為每股預先資助選擇權40.99999美元（稱為"2025年10月發行"）。預先資助的選擇權每股行使價格為0.00001美元，且可立即行使。扣除經理人折扣及佣金後，本次發行的總淨資金為3.241億美元，並扣除預估的發行費用。
自成立以來，我們已產生顯著的營運虧損。我們能否產生足夠的產品收入以實現盈利，將嚴重取決於我們能否成功開發並最終商業化任何可能開發的計畫。我們在2025年12月31日結止的會計年度內產生淨虧損2.558億美元。截至2025年12月31日，我們累計虧損為5.618億美元。我們預期在可預見的未來，若持續經營業務，將繼續產生顯著增加的費用。

全球總體經濟環境不確定，可能受到多種因素的負面影響，包括財務市場波動與不確定性、通貨膨脹、利率波動、變動的關稅政策與貿易限制、聯邦預算與債務上限的不確定性及相關潛在政府停擺、全球銀行體系的不穩定、網路安全事件、戰爭或軍事衝突的影響，包括世界各地的區域衝突，以及公共衛生大流行。我們密切監測這些因素對我們業務各方面的影響，包括對我們臨牀試驗、供應鏈、監管互動、員工、第三方夥伴、供應商及經銷商的潛在影響。全球及國內經濟條件對我們業務的最終影響仍非常不確定，將取決於未來發展及持續演變的因素。因此，我們面臨持續的風險與不確定性，並持續密切監測當前條件對我們業務的影響。有關這些風險與不確定性的更多資訊，請參閱本年度報告中標題為"風險因素"的章節。
本公司尚未自產品銷售中產生任何收入，且不預期在數年內（若有的話）自產品銷售中產生任何收入。若本公司對其計畫的開發工作成功，並取得監管機構批准或與第三方簽訂合作或授權協議，本公司未來可能自產品銷售或合作或授權協議中獲得收入，或任何組合方式。
本公司營運費用包含（i）研究與開發費用，以及（ii）一般及行政費用。
研究與開發費用主要為與本公司計畫的開發與研究相關之費用。這些費用包含：
• 開發及驗證本公司用於預臨牀研究及目前與未來臨牀試驗之製造流程的成本；
• 維持目前研究計畫及預臨牀開發任何可能識別之計畫所產生之費用，包括根據與第三方之協議（如顧問與承包商）所產生之費用；
• 資助第三方（包括 Paragon）進行研究與開發及預臨牀或臨牀活動之費用；

我們從臨牀試驗中公佈的初步、"topline" 或中期數據可能隨著更多受試者數據的取得而改變，且這些數據會經審計及驗證程序。
我們可能將有限資源用於追蹤某個特定方案，而未能把握可能更獲利或成功機率更高的方案。
我們某些方案可能與我們其他方案競爭，這可能會對我們業務造成負面影響，並降低我們未來收入。
我們正在進行且可能未來在美國境外進行我們方案之臨牀試驗，且美國食品藥物管理局（FDA）可能不會接受在這些地點進行之試驗數據。
paragraphs: 投資本公司的普通股涉及高度風險。在您決定投資本公司普通股之前，應仔細考慮下列所描述的風險，以及本年度報告中包含的其他資訊，包括「管理層對財務狀況與營運結果之討論與分析」及我們經審計之合併財務報表及其相關附註。我們認為下列所描述的風險為截至本年度報告日對我們而言具有重大影響的風險。部分因素、事件及潛在情況可能已發生於過去，但下列披露並非表示這些因素、事件或潛在情況是否已發生於過去，而是反映我們對可能對我們未來造成重大且不利影響的因素、事件或潛在情況的信念與觀點。如果任何下列風險實際發生，將可能對我們的業務、財務狀況、營運結果及未來成長前景造成重大且不利的影響。在這種情況下，本公司普通股的市場價格可能下跌，您可能損失全部或部分投資。
